selection.reason: The front bumper's fascia, absorber and lower stiffener directly decide the lower/upper legform impact results required for M1 pedestrian protection.
This global technical regulation sets the harmonised pedestrian legform test procedures for M1 bumpers, which the bumper energy-management design must meet.
The bumper is the front protective device of an M1 vehicle, and its behaviour in low-speed collisions is regulated.
The fascia, grille, plate holder, sensor housings and towing cover form external projections of an M1 car and must meet the radius and projection limits.
The bumper beam and lower stiffener are part of the front crash structure, so they affect the outcome of the M1 frontal offset impact test.
The bumper energy-management structure contributes to the crash pulse in the full-width frontal impact test of M1 vehicles.
The bumper integrates electronic sub-assemblies (radar, LIDAR with heating, camera, PDC, thermal sensor, keyless aerial, lighting), and these must meet EMC emission and immunity requirements.
The integrated side signalling lamps (e.g. direction indicators, position, side-marker or daytime running lamps) are light-signalling devices requiring component approval.

The signalling and functional lamps integrated in the bumper must be installed in the positions, visibility angles and orientations required for M1 vehicles, and decorative lighting must meet R48's restrictions.
The EV charge port housed in the bumper must meet the electric power train safety requirements, such as protection against direct contact at the charging inlet.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): Functional lighting in a front bumper typically means front fog or cornering lamps, which require road-illumination device approval.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The front radar and camera carried by the bumper are the forward-detection sensors of an M1 AEBS, if the vehicle uses them for emergency braking.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The bumper sensors may feed driver control assistance systems on M1 vehicles.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The forward detection means (radar, PDC) in the bumper may be used for acceleration control for pedal error on automatic M1 cars.
verworfen (nur Fahrzeugebene): The ECU-based sensors and keyless-entry aerial in the bumper fall within the vehicle's cyber-security scope.
verworfen (Annahme, nicht in der Spec): The software-bearing sensor ECUs in the bumper may receive software updates, which must be managed under the vehicle's software update management system.
Direction indicator provisions are consolidated into UN R148, which is selected instead.
Position and stop lamp provisions are consolidated into UN R148.
This regulation concerns rear-end collision behaviour, whereas the specification covers a front bumper.
The AEBS regulation covers M2, M3, N2 and N3 only; for M1, UN R152 applies.
This regulation has been superseded by UN R161, R162 and R163, and a keyless-entry aerial is not itself an anti-theft or alarm device.
